description: Slash commands exposed by RedOps skills for supported CLI clients.

commands.name: redops-rag
commands.description: Route an authorized task through the RedOps orchestrator and source-grounded RAG.
commands.content: Act as the RedOps orchestrator for $ARGUMENTS. Load the native Herdr/OpenCode orchestration skills, confirm the phase-gated lifecycle, retrieve source-grounded context from the read-only RAG MCP or local references, and delegate each phase to the matching specialist agent in a separate Herdr tab. Stop active phases until written scope and exact approval are confirmed. Pass each worker only its scoped evidence and handoff contract, preserve [S#] citations and source URLs, and never claim a command ran without its output. Execution remains Exegol-first and belongs to the approved phase specialist; no RedOps CLI command is required.

commands.name: engagement-workflow
commands.description: Build a phase-gated RedOps engagement plan for an authorized task.
commands.content: Use the `engagement-workflow` skill. Call `plan_engagement` first, then `route_task` for niche agents. Keep exploitation, post-exploitation, and lateral movement blocked until written scope and exact approval are confirmed. Preserve source citations and handoff artifacts; never claim execution without command output. Task: $ARGUMENTS

commands.name: solve
commands.description: Start a phase-gated RedOps engagement and coordinate scoped specialists.
commands.content: Act as the RedOps orchestrator for $ARGUMENTS. Call `plan_engagement` first, then `route_task`; confirm written scope, exact target allowlists, phase approvals and Exegol health; use engagements/<name>/notes.md as the handoff ledger; delegate only scoped evidence to recon, web-recon, web-exploit, cve-research, ad-enum, ad-exploit, linux-privesc, windows-privesc and persistence. Keep active phases blocked until their gates are satisfied and never claim a command ran without output.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Show RedOps, RAG and Exegol readiness without exposing secrets.
commands.content: Inspect the active Herdr workspace, OpenCode specialist tabs, Exegol reachability, RAG/reference availability, and the capability policy in agents/registry.yaml. Report readiness gaps without exposing credentials. Do not start scans, mutate targets, or infer authorization from runtime health.

commands.name: mobile-vuln-hunt
commands.content: Load and follow the `mobile-vuln-hunt` skill for this task. Restrict work to authorized Android/iOS artifacts and disposable lab devices; begin with static analysis and cite RedOps knowledge sources.

commands.name: reverse-engineer
commands.description: Static reverse-engineering workflow for authorized artifacts.
commands.content: Load and follow the `reverse-engineer` skill for this task. Preserve input hashes, work on copies, and do not execute unknown samples on the host. Use Exegol or bounded tools when runtime analysis is explicitly authorized.

commands.name: afl-fuzzing
commands.content: Load and follow the `afl-fuzzing` skill for this task. Fuzz only an authorized disposable Android emulator/device, validate harness reachability with a positive control, and stop when the device or scope is unavailable.
